name: Example: Parametrizing Part of a Horizontal Hyperbola
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/6e12d114aedfd6c5c8ab5830e052fcc1dd3c937b825665a0490b42ca0c87972c.png)

The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x = \sqrt2\sec{t}, \qquad y = \sqrt3\tan{t}.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x= \sqrt2 \sec{t}, \quad
y = \sqrt3 \tan{t}, \quad
t \in [-\pi,\pi], \quad
t \neq \pm\dfrac{\pi}2.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/730325137cfca58eb17d65103e539d084f81d7ab810628261125c29dbb8a0284.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}2\right)$ we get the required quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x= \sqrt2\sec{t}, \quad
y = \sqrt3\tan{t}, \quad
t \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}2\right).
$$
